reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in the disjunction between syntactic validity and semantic correctness in LLM-generated SQL. Even when an LLM produces syntactically correct queries, its inability to interpret domain-specific logic—such as player performance over time or team dynamics—results in semantically incorrect outputs. This discrepancy manifests in low DMA scores despite high execution accuracy. CricBench addresses this by introducing a benchmark that evaluates both syntactic and semantic fidelity within a specialized domain. The inclusion of multilingual support further complicates the task, as it demands consistent interpretation across linguistic boundaries. The failure mode arises when models rely solely on surface-level pattern matching instead of internalizing domain rules. This leads to a fundamental mismatch between user intent and system output, undermining trust in automated analytics systems.
